title: How the caller marks cycles
question: Which rule marks cycles: by chromatogram, by phase, or by series?
options: By chromatogram: each chromatogram is one cycle.
By phase: the UNICORN phase that starts each cycle, optionally also the phase that ends it.
By series: across results, the scouting series counts as cycles.
proposed: The caller gives one of the three rules. Cycles are never found on their own.

title: Name of the cycle flag and options key
question: What are the CLI flag and the options JSON key for the cycle rule called?
options: A name still to be chosen for the CLI flag.
A name still to be chosen for the options JSON key.
proposed: none stated

title: Settings across a chromatogram cut
question: Do flow, %B, valves, phase and state carry over a New Chromatogram cut unrepeated?
options: Take them from the previous chromatogram (hard to read, not built until a sample shows it).
Treat them as not_known before the first instruction of the next run log.
proposed: not_known before the first instruction, until a sample shows otherwise.

title: A UNICORN phase across the cut
question: How is a phase handled when the next run log starts inside it?
options: One operation in both chromatograms.
Display keeps one table set per chromatogram, noting a phase cut at the boundary.
proposed: none stated

title: Steps level (Decide 1)
question: Is there a steps level in the PyCORN batch history, or only a display table?
options: Not a level: the batch history goes down to sections, people get a display steps table.
A steps level below the phase in the batch history.
proposed: Not a level: ISA-88 ends at the phase. People get a display steps table, <c>_steps.csv or as named.

title: Words below the phase
question: What do the batch history and the display call the levels below the phase?
options: A: sections in the batch history, 'steps' in display with a note that they are not IEC steps.
B: sections in the batch history, another word in display (the owner's choice).
C: IEC steps (instructions at one breakpoint grouped), then sections inside them. Display as A or B.
proposed: none stated. C matches the standard best but waits for a check of the method against the run log.

title: Ramp length (Decide 20)
question: Which ramp length does the batch history hold: logged, measured, or both?
options: set_point: the logged length.
actual: measured on each axis.
Both, with display showing the actual.
proposed: Both: set_point (logged length) and actual (measured on each axis). Display shows the actual.

title: Repeated phases (Decide 23)
question: How are repeated phases named in display and tables?
options: instance numbers, display shows Equilibration (2), the logged text is kept.
Tables keep the logged name unchanged (today).
proposed: instance numbers. Display shows Equilibration (2). The logged text is kept.

title: Phase length with or without pauses (Decide 12)
question: Does display show phase length with pauses, without pauses, or both?
options: Phase length with pauses.
Phase length without pauses.
Both.
proposed: Both.

title: Which flow users see (Decide 15)
question: Which flow does display show: the set flow or the delivered flow?
options: The set flow, as today (Decide 6 keeps the set flow in display).
The flow the pump delivered, from the volume axis.
proposed: none stated

title: Feed wording (Decide 17)
question: What words does display use for the feed sections?
options: The wording in RUN_STRUCTURE_REVIEW.md, Decide 17.
Another wording, the owner's choice.
proposed: none stated

title: Gradient wording rule (Decide 21)
question: What rule words a gradient or ramp in display?
options: The rule in RUN_STRUCTURE_REVIEW.md, Decide 21.
Another rule, the owner's choice.
proposed: none stated

title: Section-lane chart (Decide 25)
question: Is a section-lane chart added to the display?
options: Add the section-lane chart.
Do not add it.
proposed: none stated

title: Summary beside or instead of sequences (Decide 26)
question: Does the new summary sit beside today's sequences or replace them?
options: Beside today's sequences.
Instead of today's sequences.
proposed: none stated

title: Loop and path volume flags (Decide 19)
question: Is the CADET feed volume one flag or two: --loop-volume and --sample-path-volume?
options: One flag.
Two flags: --loop-volume and --sample-path-volume.
proposed: none stated

title: The individual column
question: Where does the individual column ID come from, and what does ColumnIndividualData hold when filled?
options: From UNICORN, when ColumnIndividualData or another field stores it.
From the caller.
proposed: From UNICORN when stored, else from the caller. Needs an example from a system that tracks columns.

title: Volumes needed for dynamic binding capacity
question: Does display need total liquid and void volume for DBC, or does CADET compute DBC?
options: Display needs both volumes for DBC.
If CADET computes DBC, only CADET needs them.
proposed: none stated

title: Scope of buffer provenance and components
question: How much buffer provenance and component data does PyCORN hold?
options: IDs only (lot, recipe).
IDs with the values a model needs (composition with its kind, measured properties).
The whole chain (raw-material lots, preparation records, test results with limits).
proposed: none stated. A LIMS, ELN or MES already holds the whole chain.

title: Scope of component fields
question: Does the batch history hold component fields and compositions, or only link to them by ID?
options: Hold the fields (identifier, form, molecular weight, basis, role, assay, model component), solution properties and compositions.
Only link to them by ID.
proposed: none stated. Physicochemical constants are out of scope (D28).

title: Order of composition values for CADET
question: Does CADET take as-made before the recipe target by a fixed order or by the caller's choice per run?
options: A fixed order: as made where given, else the recipe's target.
The caller's choice per run.
proposed: As made where given, else the recipe's target (proposed, the order TBD).

title: Offline volume precedence
question: When does a measured volume or mass take precedence over the volume axis, and does it apply to display too?
options: Always use UNICORN's volume axis, as for now.
A measured mass takes precedence, converted with the caller's density, for calculations.
The same precedence for display as well as calculations.
proposed: For now the volume axis is used for every calculation and display (owner, 2026-11-15). A measured mass may later take precedence.
